broker.provisioning: temporary container, --pull=never, random credentials, loopback random port, removed after the run

worker_failure_contract_on_a_real_broker.5xx: nack + requeue, then the second delivery is accepted (2 HTTP attempts, empty task queue, empty DLQ)
worker_failure_contract_on_a_real_broker.process_death: while the worker port is closed every delivery fails to connect and keeps retrying; after a new process binds the same port the message is accepted and removed
worker_failure_contract_on_a_real_broker.409_stale_or_duplicate: acknowledged once and never redelivered (1 HTTP attempt, no retry counter)
worker_failure_contract_on_a_real_broker.note: the pre-existing cases covered redelivery, mandatory return and 4xx dead-lettering; these three cover the worker-restart path that dispatch documentation promises

tooling_defect_found_and_fixed.symptom: every run failed with 'Temporary RabbitMQ did not become ready'
tooling_defect_found_and_fixed.root_cause: the readiness probe ran rabbitmq-diagnostics as root inside the container, which created a root-owned /var/lib/rabbitmq/.erlang.cookie before the entrypoint dropped privileges; the broker then crashed with 'Error when reading /var/lib/rabbitmq/.erlang.cookie: eacces' (exit code 1)
tooling_defect_found_and_fixed.evidence: container logs and inspect captured in gateway/target/rabbit-acceptance/rabbit-failure.log; container exit code 1 ~8 s after start
fix: probe with docker exec --user rabbitmq so the cookie is never created as root
replace the fixed 60-iteration poll with a 180 s wall-clock deadline plus TimeoutExpired tolerance, because a cold management image needs 15-40 s
keep the temporary container on failure and write logs plus inspect to the output directory instead of auto-removing the diagnosis
tooling_defect_found_and_fixed.note: the previous 2026-10-22 acceptance used a native broker; this run proves the same three properties against a container broker provisioned by the tool itself, so the documented command is now reproducible

limitations: Single local broker: proves delivery, confirmation, mandatory-return and dead-letter behaviour, not broker cluster failover
No multi-node quorum queue rebalance drill
Does not prove capacity or latency under production load
Python platform Worker endpoints are still required for a real end-to-end dispatch
